_meta.name: FormuSense population protein reference set
_meta.source: ICMR-NIN (2020) 'Nutrient Requirements for Indians - Recommended Dietary Allowances (RDA) and Estimated Average Requirements (EAR)'. National Institute of Nutrition, Hyderabad.

key_values.note: The 2020 revision lowered the adult protein RDA from 1.0 to 0.83 g/kg/day and set the EAR at 0.66 g/kg/day.

_meta.disclaimer: INDICATIVE reference values, transcribed for product-development guidance. They reproduce ICMR-NIN 2020 protein recommendations so a formulation team can show what one serving contributes to each population group. Entries are editable configuration: verify against the current ICMR-NIN publication (Tables 2a and 2b) before any on-pack or regulatory use. This is product-development guidance, not medical or dietetic advice.

units.rda_g_day: recommended dietary allowance, grams of protein per day for the reference body weight
units.ear_g_day: estimated average requirement, grams of protein per day
units.ref_weight_kg: reference body weight the RDA is quoted against
units.rda_g_kg_day: RDA expressed per kg body weight
units.protein_energy_pct: acceptable macronutrient distribution range for protein as a share of energy
units.practical_upper_g_kg_day: practical upper intake used as a caution flag (not a toxicological limit)

groups.label: Children 1-3 years
cautions: Small body weight: a single adult serving can exceed the whole-day requirement.
Cap added sugar and sodium; infants under 1 year are outside this profile set.

groups.label: Children 4-6 years
cautions: Serve size should stay well below the adult portion.
Watch added sugar against the day's total.

groups.label: Children 7-9 years
cautions: A high-protein product is a supplement here, not a meal replacer.

groups.label: Boys 10-12 years
cautions: Growth spurt raises demand; protein alone does not replace energy needs.

groups.label: Girls 10-12 years
cautions: Growth spurt raises demand; protein alone does not replace energy needs.

groups.label: Boys 13-15 years
cautions: Peak growth period: pair protein with adequate energy and iron.

groups.label: Girls 13-15 years
cautions: Peak growth period: pair protein with adequate energy and iron.

groups.label: Boys 16-18 years
cautions: Often the highest requirement of any group; do not dilute with an energy-only snack.

groups.label: Girls 16-18 years
cautions: Iron and energy are usually the limiting nutrients, not protein.

groups.label: Adult men (19-59 years)
cautions: Higher protein is used for muscle gain, but the RDA is the adequacy floor; a supplement is not a substitute for a mixed diet.

groups.label: Adult women (19-59 years)
cautions: Iron, calcium and folate are usually the priority nutrients alongside protein.

groups.label: Pregnant women
cautions: Additional allowance above the non-pregnant requirement; the extra need is concentrated in the second and third trimesters.
Any high-protein product in pregnancy should be used under medical guidance.
Food safety matters more here: pasteurised or shelf-stable product only; no raw-milk base.

groups.label: Lactating women
cautions: Additional allowance above the non-pregnant requirement for milk production.
Use under medical guidance; hydration and total energy matter as much as protein.

groups.label: Men 60+ years
cautions: ICMR-NIN quotes the adult RDA; evidence on sarcopenia supports a higher 1.0-1.2 g/kg/day target for older adults, shown alongside as guidance.
Distribute protein across meals rather than in one serving.
Renal impairment changes protein advice: defer to a clinician.

groups.label: Women 60+ years
cautions: ICMR-NIN quotes the adult RDA; evidence on sarcopenia supports a higher 1.0-1.2 g/kg/day target for older adults, shown alongside as guidance.
Distribute protein across meals rather than in one serving.
Renal impairment changes protein advice: defer to a clinician.
